title: Paraphrase drill: Savings account or TFSA?
context: You will hear a customer talking to a representative at a credit union about where to keep her savings. The interest rates are fictional.

segments.speaker: Mai
segments.text: Hi. I've got about eight thousand dollars sitting in my chequing account, and my friend says I'm basically wasting it. I'm trying to decide between your high-interest savings account and a TFSA.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: Your friend's right, chequing pays almost nothing. So, the high-interest savings account pays three point one percent right now. You can put in as much as you like and take money out any time, no fees.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: The catch is that the interest counts as income, so you pay tax on it.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: Our TFSA savings account pays a bit less, two point seven five percent. But whatever it earns is tax-free. You never report it on your tax return.

segments.speaker: Mai
segments.text: Oh, so even with the lower rate, I might end up with more.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: For a lot of people, yes, especially if you're in a higher tax bracket. The thing to watch is your contribution room. There's a yearly limit set by the government, and if you go over it, there's a penalty of one percent a month on the extra amount.

segments.speaker: Mai
segments.text: How do I know my limit? I moved to Canada in twenty twenty-one.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: You'd check your CRA My Account online. Your room started building the year you became a resident, so you probably have plenty for eight thousand. But please check before you deposit.

segments.speaker: Mai
segments.text: Okay. And if I need the money for, say, an emergency?

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: You can withdraw from the TFSA any time. Just know that the amount you take out only gets added back to your room the following January.

segments.speaker: Samuel
segments.text: So if you take out two thousand in March and put it back in June, that could cause an over-contribution.

segments.speaker: Mai
segments.text: Wow, that's a trap I'd definitely fall into.

questions.prompt: What is the main disadvantage of the high-interest savings account?

options.text: There is a fee for each withdrawal.
options.whyVi: Rút tiền bất cứ lúc nào, 'no fees'.

options.text: The money it earns is taxable.
options.whyVi: Đúng: tiền lãi tính là thu nhập nên phải đóng thuế.

options.text: There is a limit on how much you can deposit.
options.whyVi: Giới hạn đóng góp là của TFSA; tài khoản này 'put in as much as you like'.

options.text: It pays less interest than the TFSA.
options.whyVi: Tài khoản này lãi cao hơn (3,1% so với 2,75%).

questions.evidence: The catch is that the interest counts as income, so you pay tax on it.
questions.explanationVi: 'The catch' = điểm bất lợi. 'Interest counts as income, so you pay tax on it' được diễn đạt lại thành 'the money it earns is taxable'.

questions.prompt: What does Mai realize about the TFSA?

options.text: It could leave her better off despite its lower interest rate.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'even with the lower rate, I might end up with more'.

options.text: It pays a higher rate than the savings account.
She must report its interest on her tax return.
options.whyVi: Lãi TFSA miễn thuế, 'You never report it'.

options.text: It is only worth it for people in a high tax bracket.
options.whyVi: Samuel nói 'especially' với người thuế suất cao, không phải 'only'.

questions.evidence: Oh, so even with the lower rate, I might end up with more.
questions.explanationVi: 'End up with more' = cuối cùng có nhiều tiền hơn, tức là 'better off'. 'Even with the lower rate' = 'despite its lower interest rate'.

questions.prompt: What happens if Mai puts in more than her TFSA limit?

options.whyVi: Không ai nói tài khoản bị đóng.

options.text: She will lose all the interest she has earned.
She will pay one percent a year on her whole balance.
options.whyVi: Phạt 1% MỖI THÁNG và chỉ trên phần vượt, không phải mỗi năm trên toàn bộ số dư.

options.text: She will be charged a monthly penalty on the excess amount.
options.whyVi: Đúng: phạt 1% mỗi tháng trên số tiền vượt mức.

questions.evidence: if you go over it, there's a penalty of one percent a month on the extra amount
questions.explanationVi: 'Go over it' = vượt giới hạn; 'the extra amount' = 'the excess amount'; 'one percent a month' = phạt hằng tháng.

questions.prompt: What does Samuel explain about taking money out of a TFSA?

options.text: Withdrawals are only allowed in January.
options.whyVi: 'January' là lúc hạn mức được cộng lại; rút tiền được bất cứ lúc nào.

options.text: Money withdrawn can be put back right away without any problem.
options.whyVi: Gửi lại ngay trong cùng năm có thể gây vượt mức đóng góp.

options.text: The room used by a withdrawal is only restored the next year.
options.whyVi: Đúng: số tiền rút ra chỉ được cộng lại vào hạn mức vào tháng Một năm sau.

options.text: There is a two-thousand-dollar limit on withdrawals.
options.whyVi: 2.000 đô chỉ là ví dụ, không phải giới hạn rút tiền.

questions.evidence: Just know that the amount you take out only gets added back to your room the following January.
questions.explanationVi: 'Gets added back to your room the following January' = hạn mức được khôi phục vào năm sau. Ví dụ rút tháng Ba, gửi lại tháng Sáu minh họa cho bẫy này.

vocabulary.example: The catch is that you pay tax on the interest.
Interest earned in a TFSA is tax-free.

vocabulary.definition: to have something as a final result
vocabulary.example: Even at a lower rate, you might end up with more.

vocabulary.definition: a range of income taxed at a particular rate
vocabulary.example: It helps more if you're in a higher tax bracket.

vocabulary.definition: the amount you are allowed to put into a registered account
vocabulary.example: Check your contribution room before you deposit.

vocabulary.definition: to take money out of an account
vocabulary.example: You can withdraw from the TFSA at any time.

vocabulary.definition: putting in more than your allowed limit
vocabulary.example: Putting the money back too soon could cause an over-contribution.

review.notes: Blind-solved all 4 Qs; key matched; all 4 paraphrase. TFSA facts verified: 1%/month on excess, room accrues from year of residency (18+), withdrawals restored the following Jan 1, HISA interest taxable; rates flagged as fictional. No changes needed.
